rows.text: Why it sits here. Each Trump is a path on the Tree of Life, carried by a Hebrew letter ({letter}) and its attribution ({attribution}). So Atu {atu} inherits every correspondence of Key {key} — its colour, perfume, and plane of consciousness all follow from that path.
rows.note: Tarot Deck: a trump's page, under its correspondences. {letter}: the Hebrew letter of its path; {attribution}: the path's element, planet or sign; {atu}: the trump's number (Golden Dawn order, as the deck lists it); {key}: its 777 row.

rows.text: Why it sits here. The ten numbered cards are the ten Sephiroth in the four worlds: the {rank} = Sephira {n} ({sephira_meaning}) in the World of {element} ({suit}). Its title names how that sphere's force expresses through this element{decans}.

rank
n
sephira_meaning
element
suit
decans
rows.note: Tarot Deck: the page of an Ace to Ten. {rank}: Ace, 2 … 10; {n}: its number; {sephira_meaning}: 777 col. III of that Sephira; {element}: the suit's element; {suit}: the suit; {decans}: the text tarot.why-small-decans for the 2 to 10, nothing for an Ace.

rows.text: ; the 2–10 also map to the decans ruled by planets in the suit’s three signs
rows.note: Put in at {decans} in tarot.why-small, for the 2 to 10 (before its final full stop).

rows.text: Why it sits here. The court is built from the elements: each suit is one element ({suit} = {suit_element}), and its four figures are the four elements within it — {figures}. So the {rank} of {suit} is the {element} of {suit_element}, and it also rules a span of the zodiac (the last decan of one sign + first two of the next).
rows.note: Tarot Deck: the page of a court card. {figures}: each rank with its element (Knight/King = Fire, …: the Court ranks tab); {rank}: the card's rank (Thoth / Book T name); {element}: the rank's element; {suit_element}: the suit's.

rows.text:
Tap a path (the lettered lines) to see the letter, its Tarot Atu, the sign or planet it carries, and its full column of correspondences — or tap a numbered sphere for a Sephira. Use the scale buttons to paint the tree in the {scales} colours (each still labelled, colour-blind safe).

† Consciousness of the Adept (Col. IV) is authored here — the book leaves it blank but for the veil הוא; these entries are an editorial synthesis grounded in the Qabalistic tradition, not Crowley's text.
rows.note: Tree of Life: the panel before anything is tapped. {scales}: the names of the four colour scales (King/Queen/Emperor/Empress: the Suits tab, column scale_name).

rows.text: Minutum Mundum — {scale} scale. Colours are labelled on click with exact RGB (colour-blind safe).
rows.note: Tree of Life: under the tree while it is coloured by a scale (plain text). {scale}: King, Queen …

rows.text: Rosicrucian grade ladder (Col. CXXI) — each sphere is a plane of consciousness/attainment: {lowest_sphere} = {lowest_grade}, ascending to {highest_sphere} = {highest_grade}.
rows.note: Tree of Life: under the tree while the grades are shown (plain text). The grades are 777 col. CXXI: {lowest_grade} is the last grade of Malkuth's cell, {highest_grade} the grade of Kether's.

rows.text: Book T and Crowley read the cards upright and use elemental dignities instead of reversals
rows.note: Spread Reader: the tip on the "allow reversed" switch (plain text).

rows.text: Tap a Key-Scale row, or search above. Everything works offline.

rows.text: the hour of {planet} on that day — see the Planetary Hours tool

rows.text: How to read this. The whole recipe hangs off one place on the Tree ({place}). Assemble the working in its colour, burn its incense, invoke under its god-name and angels, on its planet's day and hour, using its tarot card and number as focus. The "aim" is the state that place confers. † Timing (day + hour) is the layer the talismanic tradition leans on most — pair this with the Planetary Hours tool.
rows.note: Working Designer: under each recipe. {place}: the Sephira or path of the intent.

rows.text: ⚠︎ Moon void-of-course at noon — traditionally a poor time to begin ventures.

rows.text: ✓ Moon not void-of-course at noon.
rows.note: Moon & Timing: in the same place when it is not.

rows.text: Void-of-course = the Moon makes no further aspect to the seven classical planets before leaving {sign}; a traditional caution for elections. Checked at noon UT.

rows.text: Geocentric tropical positions from a compact ephemeris (JPL Keplerian elements + truncated lunar theory). Ingress times are approximate (typically within an hour or two) and shown in your device’s local time. ℞ = retrograde.

rows.note: Sky & Transits: a search result's dignity, labelled Detriment, when it is in its detriment there (tab Dignities). Put in at {dignity} in sky.reading.

rows.text: in fall — humbled; its expression turns inward and subtle.

rows.text: Stamps computed on the phone at the first keystroke of each entry: tropical zodiac, compact ephemeris; unequal planetary hours (sunrise to sunset and sunset to sunrise, each in twelve), Chaldean order; essential dignities, Atus and keywords after “{sheet}”; decans are the Thoth small cards 2–10.
rows.note: Daily Journal: the footer of each day's file. {sheet}: the title of the dignity sheet (tab Texts, dignities.title).

rows.note: Daily Journal: under the sky snapshot of a stamp. {outer}: the outer planets (tab Planets, kind outer), e.g. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto.

rows.text: Tropical zodiac · positions accurate to a few arc-minutes (1800–2050) · Ascendant & MC need time + place. If a body sits within ~0.1° of a sign cusp, verify with a full ephemeris. {outer} use the modern attributions to Keys {outer_keys}.
rows.note: Sign Chart Calculator: the small print under the form. {outer}: the outer planets (tab Planets, kind outer); {outer_keys}: their 777 rows (the path of each one's element), e.g. 11 / 23 / 31.

rows.text: Zodiac runs counter-clockwise with the Ascendant at left (9 o’clock) and the MC toward the top. Aspect lines: solid = opposition, long-dash = square, dotted = trine/sextile (patterns, not colour). Whole-sign houses count from the Ascendant's sign.
rows.note: Sign Chart Calculator: under the chart wheel.

rows.text: Dignities tell how comfortably a planet works in its sign: {domicile} (home/strong), {exaltation} (elevated), {detriment} (opposite of home), {fall} (opposite of exaltation), Peregrine (neutral).
rows.note: Sign Chart Calculator: under the Placements table. {domicile} … {fall}: the four dignities as the table labels them (tab Dignity kinds: short_label, else name).

rows.text: Aspects are the angles between bodies — the geometry of how they combine. Tighter orb (nearer exact) = stronger. {conjunction} fuse, {sextile}/{trine} flow easily, {square}/{opposition} create tension that drives growth.
rows.note: Sign Chart Calculator: under the Aspects table. {conjunction} … {opposition}: the aspects' glyphs (tab Aspects).

rows.text: A planetary talisman concentrates the virtue of a planet into a seal. The method is the same for each: elect the planet’s day and hour (Planetary Hours tab) with the Moon in the matching tide (Moon & Timing tab) — waxing to draw, waning to bind or banish — then name your intent, charge the seal in its incense, and keep or seal it as its rite directs.
rows.note: Talismans: the paragraph at the top of the page.

rows.text: Elect the moment with the Planetary Hours and Moon & Timing tabs. Treat binding-work soberly, and know how to release it.
rows.note: Talismans: the line at the foot of the page.

rows.text: The screen stays on while the app is open. You can also lock the phone during a session — the metronome keeps playing (a “Breathwork in progress” notification with a Stop button shows while it runs), so you can follow it with your eyes closed.

rows.text: Tap letters to build a word, or type a number to find every name in the 777 table with that value.

rows.text: What gematria is. Each Hebrew letter is also a number, so every word carries a sum. Two words with the same sum are traditionally read as secretly connected — the classic example, אחד (Unity) and אהבה (Love) both = 13, and יהוה = 26 = twice 13. Use it to find the table-names that resonate with a word or number.
rows.note: Gematria tab: the explanation under a word's or number's value.

rows.text: {count} name(s) in the 777 table also total {value} — words of equal value are held to share a hidden kinship:
rows.note: Gematria tab: over the list of names of equal value. {count}: how many; {value}: the value (both in the chosen numerals).

rows.text: The Rose Cross method. The 22 Hebrew letters are set on a rose — 3 mothers innermost, 7 doubles in the middle ring, 12 singles outermost. To make a sigil you draw a line from letter to letter spelling your word: a small circle marks the first letter, a short bar caps the last. The result is a single glyph condensing the name — used as a focus in ritual or on a talisman.
rows.note: Rose Cross sigil tab: under the rose. (Which letters are mothers, doubles and singles follows their attribution in the Key scale tab.)

rows.text: The Kamea (magic-square) method. Each planet has a magic square where every row, column and diagonal sums alike. To sigilise a name you take each Hebrew letter's value, reduce it into the square's range (1–{max}) by subtracting {max} as many times as needed, and connect those numbered cells in order — a circle on the first, a bar on the last. This is the classical way planetary talisman sigils are drawn (Agrippa, Key of Solomon).
rows.note: Planetary sigil tab: under the square (then 'Letters reduced to: …'). {max}: the square's last number (size × size; tab Kameas).

rows.text: Tap letters to build an Arabic word, or type a number to find Hebrew names in the table with that value.
rows.note: Arabic (Abjad) tab: the hint under the letter keyboard.

rows.text: {count} Hebrew name(s) in the 777 table also total {value} — Abjad and Hebrew gematria share one number-scale, so an Arabic word can be read against the Hebrew Tree:
rows.note: Arabic (Abjad) tab: over the list of Hebrew names of equal value. {count}: how many; {value}: the value.

rows.text: Arabic gematria (Abjad / ḥisāb al-jummal). The 28 Arabic letters each carry a number, following the old order أبجد هوز حطي كلمن سعفص قرشت ثخذ ضظغ. The first 22 match the Hebrew values exactly (ا=1 like א, ب=2 like ב…); six extra letters run 500–1000. Values here use the standard Eastern (Mashriqī) order — a Western (Maghribī) order gives six letters different values. Hamza-forms count as their carrier, ة as 5, ى as 10, and vowel-marks (ḥarakāt) as 0.
rows.note: Arabic (Abjad) tab: the explanation under a word's value. (The letters and values themselves: tab Arabic letters.)

rows.text: The Wafq (talismanic magic square). Islamic magic fills the planetary squares with letters (abjad numerals), not digits — every row, column and diagonal summing alike is held to bind the planet's virtue. To sigilise a name you reduce each Arabic letter's abjad value into 1–{max} and join those cells, a circle on the first and a bar on the last — the same awfāq tradition (al-Būnī, the Picatrix) that Agrippa later borrowed.
rows.note: Arabic Wafq & Buduh tab: under the square. {max}: the square's last number (in abjad letters when 'abjad letters' is ticked).

rows.text: This {size} is the famous {name} square: its highlighted corners {digits} = {letters} spell {arabic}, itself worn as a charm for protection, travel and childbirth.
rows.note: Arabic Wafq & Buduh tab: added after gem.wafq for a square with a name of its own (tab Kameas: wafq_name, Saturn's Buduh). {size}: 3×3; {name}, {arabic}: its name; {letters}: the name's letters; {digits}: their values in Eastern digits, which are the highlighted cells.

rows.text: The Seven Seals (al-khawātim as-sabʿa). Given in al-Būnī’s Shams al-Maʿārif (13th c.), the seven signs are held to unlock the Greatest Name of God (ism Allāh al-aʿẓam); they are aligned with the seven planets and days and written together on amulets (ḥijāb) for protection, and appended after certain Qur’anic verses. Important: the exact shapes — and their day/planet order — differ between manuscripts and printings; this is one common rendition offered for study, not a single authoritative form.
rows.note: Seven Seals tab: under the table of seals (tab Seals of Solomon).

rows.text: Pathworking is a guided journey of the imagination along one of the 22 paths that join the ten spheres (Sephiroth) of the Tree of Life. Each path is a Hebrew letter, a tarot trump and an astrological force. You sit quietly, build in your mind the temple of the sphere you start from, and pass through a veil painted with the path's trump. The trump is the doorway. Then you walk the path, noticing what you see and whom you meet, and return the way you came.
rows.note: Pathworking, Home: the first paragraph under 'What is pathworking?'.

rows.text: The Golden Dawn called this skrying in the spirit vision, and Crowley's students did the same work. The aim is to know the correspondences from the inside, not only that Samekh is Sagittarius and blue but what that path feels like, and to train the imagination and the will so that images arise clearly and can be held and steered.
rows.note: Pathworking, Home: the second paragraph under 'What is pathworking?'.

rows.text: Tradition climbs from Malkuth: begin with path 32 (Tau), take one path at a time, and leave days or weeks between journeys so each one can settle.
rows.note: Pathworking, Home: the third paragraph under 'What is pathworking?'.

rows.text: Stay safe. Banish before and after, ground yourself afterwards (eat something, stamp your feet), keep a journal, and stop at once if you feel distressed. You can always open your eyes.
rows.note: Pathworking, Home: the note at the end of 'What is pathworking?'.

rows.text:
• Tap a path on the Tree (the next one in the climb is highlighted) and read its page. Its correspondences are the landmarks you should expect to meet.
  • Prepare the room with the checklist, then press Begin journey.
  • Each step appears on screen and can be read aloud. Read it, close your eyes and hold the vision during the silence; a soft bell calls you back.
  • Afterwards, record what happened. Tick the expected symbols that appeared on their own: a rough check that you were on the path you meant to walk.
rows.note:
Pathworking, Home: the numbered steps under 'How to use this tool' (one
  • …
    • per step).

rows.text: The Tunnels of Set are the averse, shadow side of the paths. The genii of the tunnels are named in Crowley's Liber 231; Kenneth Grant developed them as the Tunnels of Set in Nightside of Eden. They are not part of Liber 777. When shown, each path page adds a card for contemplation, not invocation. Work the day-side path first.
rows.note: Pathworking, Home: under the switch 'Show the Nightside (Tunnels of Set)'.

rows.text: Correspondences: Liber 777 · Tunnels: Nightside workbook data · Moon phases computed on the device.
rows.note: Pathworking, Home: the line at the foot of the page.

rows.text: Crowley: “Tzaddi is not the Star” (Liber AL I:57). In the Thoth Tarot The Star (Aquarius) goes to Hé, path 15, and The Emperor (Aries) to Tzaddi, path 28; the letters stay where they are. The correspondences below follow the sign, so they are read from Liber 777's {sign} row, which the book prints under {row_letter} (path {row}). The Intelligence stays with the letter. The Golden Dawn has {gd} on this path.
rows.note: Pathworking, a path's page (paths 15 and 28): the note under the heading. {sign}: the sign whose 777 row the path is read from (the Thoth trump's row); {row_letter}, {row}: that row's letter and number; {gd}: the Golden Dawn trump on this path, with its number and sign (tab Cards).

rows.text: Caution. This is for contemplation, not invocation, and there is no guided journey into the tunnels here. Walk the day-side path first, and more than once; banish before and after; if the reflection stirs fear or distress, stop, ground yourself and return to the day-side work.
rows.note: Pathworking, a path's page: the note at the end of the Nightside card.

rows.text: Tick the expected symbols that appeared on their own. One that arrived unbidden counts for more than one you placed deliberately.
rows.note: Pathworking, the journal form: under 'Symbols · verification'.
